18-1.title: Start with the schemes the child is actually entitled to — India has no universal child benefit
18-1.inPlainWords: India does not pay a universal per-child cash benefit. The support is a patchwork: PM-JAY health cover for an eligible household, ICDS anganwadi services, PM POSHAN meals at school, the state maternity benefit, and some state child-benefit schemes. Check the eligibility and the local office. A private 'benefit agent' is not needed.
18-1.benefit: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY covers hospitalisation for eligible households. The Integrated Child Development Services provides supplementary nutrition and pre-school at an anganwadi. PM POSHAN provides a school meal. The Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana provides a maternity benefit for an eligible woman. State governments run additional schemes, so the district social welfare office is the place to ask.
18-1.cost: The central schemes are free. A state scheme may have an income limit.
18-1.caveats: Eligibility is based on the SECC and state lists, not on a self-declaration. A scheme can change with the state government. Do not pay an agent to 'apply' for a free scheme.
18-1.sources: National Health Authority, PM-JAY. <https://nha.gov.in/>; Ministry of Women and Child Development, ICDS. <https://wcd.gov.in/>; Ministry of Education, PM POSHAN. <https://www.education.gov.in/>; Ministry of Rural Development. <https://rural.nic.in/>

18-2.title: Maternity leave is 26 weeks for the first two children, and the employer pays the benefit
18-2.cost: No cost to the employee. The employer pays the maternity benefit; where the woman is an insured person, the Employees' State Insurance Corporation pays it in place of the employer.
18-2.inPlainWords: If your establishment is covered by the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, you get 26 weeks of paid maternity leave for the first two children, and 12 weeks after that. The leave may begin up to eight weeks before the expected date of delivery. A woman who adopts a child below three months of age, or who has a child through surrogacy, gets 12 weeks. The benefit is paid at your average daily wage for the days you actually worked in the three months before the leave. The employer may also let you work from home after the 26 weeks, on terms you both agree.
18-2.benefit: The Act also requires a crèche in every establishment with 50 or more employees, and two nursing breaks in addition to the usual interval until the child is 15 months old. You must give the employer notice of the leave and of the expected date of delivery. An employer cannot dismiss you, or cut your pay, because of the leave, and a woman who is dismissed can still claim the benefit she had earned.
18-2.caveats: The Act covers factories, mines, plantations and shops or establishments with 10 or more employees, and establishments covered by the ESIC Act. If your workplace falls outside it, your protection comes from the state Shops and Establishments Act and your contract, so check both. A woman with two or more surviving children gets 12 weeks, not 26. Adoption in India runs through the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 and the Adoption Regulations, 2022. Keep the leave application, the delivery certificate and the salary slips.
18-2.sources: Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, as amended in 2017, Ministry of Labour and Employment. <https://labour.gov.in/>; Employees' State Insurance Corporation. <https://esic.gov.in/>; Ministry of Women and Child Development. <https://wcd.gov.in/>

18-3.title: An employer cannot cut your pay or dismiss you because of pregnancy, childbirth or breastfeeding
18-3.inPlainWords: Under the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 an employer cannot dismiss a woman, or reduce her pay, because she is on maternity leave or because of an absence caused by the pregnancy. A woman is also entitled to two nursing breaks, in addition to the usual rest interval, until the child is 15 months old. An employer that breaks the Act can be prosecuted, and the court may order imprisonment of up to one year, a fine, or both.
18-3.benefit: The Act places the duty on the employer and gives a woman who is denied the benefit or the nursing breaks a route to complain to the Inspector appointed under the Act and to the labour authority of the state. A dismissal connected with maternity leave does not extinguish the benefit already earned. Keep the appointment letter, the salary slips, the leave application and any message about a transfer or a pay cut.
18-3.caveats: The Act covers establishments with 10 or more employees and establishments covered by ESIC. Outside that, your protection comes from the state Shops and Establishments Act, the Industrial Relations Code, 2020 if you are a workman, or your contract. For a complaint, approach the labour inspector or the state labour department; for free legal aid, the National Legal Services Authority on 15100.
18-3.sources: Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, Ministry of Labour and Employment. <https://labour.gov.in/>; National Legal Services Authority. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>; Ministry of Women and Child Development. <https://wcd.gov.in/>

18-5.caveats: Break the cost into three periods: ages 0–3 (delivery, immunisation, childcare), the school years (fees, books, transport, PM POSHAN covers a midday meal at a government school), and after 18 (college or training, where a scholarship or an education loan may apply). Add the cost of health cover; PM-JAY covers an eligible household. A private school and a government school differ by an order of magnitude, so compare the actual fee structure, not an average.

18-7.benefit: In natural fecundability, a prospective cohort study of women aged 30–44 without history of infertility demonstrated that compared to women aged 30–31, monthly conception probability was 53% lower at ages 40–41 (fecundability ratio 0.47, 95% CI: 0.28–0.78) and 59% lower at ages 42–44 (ratio 0.39, 95% CI: 0.16–0.93); at ages 38–39, conception was 30% lower (ratio 0.70, 95% CI: 0.48–1.01), while ages 32–33 showed no difference compared to 30–31. Nulligravid women had lower fecundability across all ages. In a Danish general population cohort, women aged 35–40 had a conception ratio of 0.77 compared to ages 20–24, whereas male age had a much smaller impact (ratio 0.95 at ages 35–39). In spontaneous pregnancy loss, a Norwegian nationwide registry study of ~420,000 pregnancies found the lowest miscarriage risk at ages 25–29 (9.8%), rising to 10.8% at 30–34, 16.7% at 35–39, 32.2% at 40–44, and 53.6% past age 45. In embryonic genetics, comprehensive chromosomal screening of 15,169 consecutive IVF trophectoderm biopsies revealed that embryonic aneuploidy rates rise steadily with maternal age past 26: while 2% to 6% of cycles between ages 26 and 37 produce all-aneuploid embryos, this jumps to 33% at age 42 and 53% at age 44. In assisted reproductive outcomes, preliminary UK Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority (HFEA 2022) data showed live birth rates per fresh autologous embryo transfer of 35% for ages 18–34, 26% for 35–37, 18% for 38–39, 10% for 40–42, and 5% for 43–44. Regulatory context in India: the Assisted Reproductive Technology (Regulation) Act, 2021 and the rules made under it govern ART clinics and banks. Treatment is open to married couples and to single women, within the age limits in the Act, and a clinic must be registered and follow its conditions. ART clinics must also follow the Pre-conception and Pre-natal Diagnostic Techniques (Prohibition of Sex Selection) Act, 1994, which prohibits prenatal sex determination.
18-7.caveats: This analysis does not advocate any specific childbearing age, but presents empirical reproductive biological realities to weigh alongside financial costs (Chapter 18, Rule 5) and parental time investments (Chapter 18, Rule 4). Statistics represent population-wide averages; consult reproductive specialists for individualized ovarian reserve assessment (e.g. AMH and antral follicle counts). Public schemes generally do not cover ART, and a private policy usually excludes it, so ask the clinic for its schedule of charges and check your own policy before you start. Preconception preparations and folic acid supplementation are covered in Chapter 27, Rule 1.
